exposure: maternal glycemic profiles (HbA1c, FBG, GA, OGTT-1H results, DIP status)
cohort: The study enrolled 710 pregnant women from a population-based sample.
finding: Maternal blood glucose levels during pregnancy and predelivery significantly influence neonatal blood glucose and bilirubin levels, increasing the risk of neonatal hypoglycemia and jaundice.
mod_finding: Cesarean section delivery was linked to higher neonatal blood glucose with increased maternal predelivery glucose and a higher risk of jaundice, whereas natural delivery showed a greater influence on fetal glucose levels and had bilirubin levels correlated with maternal GA.
